newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Yanacocha Jan-Oct gold output up 57.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Yanacocha Jan-Oct gold output up 57.1 pct.

text.p: Peru's largest gold miner Minera Yanacocha S.A. produced 20.87 tonnes in the first ten months of the year, up 57.07 percent compared with the same period last year, the government said Monday.

Yanacocha, a joint venture run by Newmont Mining Corp in the northern Peruvian Andes, produced 17 tonnes of gold in 1995, up 75 percent from the previous year, and plans this year to boost output to 22 tonnes.
Yanacocha accounted for 38 percent of Peru's total output in the first ten months of the year, according to preliminary Energy and Mines Ministry figures.
Peru's gold output of 54.4 tonnes in the first ten months was up 17 percent compared with the same period last year.
This total output includes an estimated 20.4 tonnes produced by informal gold miners, mainly in Peru's southeastern jungle, southern coast and northeastern Andes.
In 1995, Peru's total gold output rose 18 percent to 56 tonnes.

Yanacocha is owned by partners Newmont and local firm Cia. Minera Buenaventura S.A., which own 51.35 percent and 43.65 percent respectively. The remaining five percent is owned by the World Bank's International Finance Corp.
The firm produces gold through heap-leaching operations at its open-pit mines in highland Cajamarca department some 375 miles (600 km) north of Lima.
